vocabulary.meaning_en: a passage between rows of shelves or seats
vocabulary.example: You'll find the rice in aisle five.
vocabulary.note_en: The letter s is silent: say /aɪl/.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small container you carry your shopping in
vocabulary.example: I only need a few things, so I'll take a basket.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the place in a shop where you pay
vocabulary.note_ar: كفعل تُكتب كلمتين: check out = يدفع ويغادر
vocabulary.example: There was a long line at the checkout.
vocabulary.note_en: As a verb it is two words: check out = pay and leave.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the person who takes your money in a shop
vocabulary.example: The cashier gave me my change.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a paper that shows what you paid
vocabulary.example: Keep the receipt in case you want to return it.
vocabulary.note_en: The letter p is silent: say /rɪˈsiːt/.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a large wheeled basket for shopping
vocabulary.note_ar: trolley أشيع في بريطانيا، cart أشيع في أمريكا وكندا
vocabulary.example: She pushed the cart to the fruit section.
vocabulary.note_en: "Trolley" is more common in Britain; "cart" is more common in the US and Canada.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an amount taken off the normal price
vocabulary.example: Students get a 10% discount here.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the name of a company's products
vocabulary.example: Which brand of coffee do you usually buy?

vocabulary.meaning_en: fresh fruit and vegetables
vocabulary.example: The fresh produce is near the entrance.
vocabulary.note_en: As a verb, "produce" means to make or grow something.

vocabulary.meaning_en: milk and foods made from milk
vocabulary.example: Cheese and yogurt are dairy products.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a place where bread and cakes are made or sold
vocabulary.example: The bakery opens at six in the morning.
vocabulary.note_en: From the verb "bake" (to cook bread or cakes in an oven).

vocabulary.meaning_en: food sold in metal containers
vocabulary.example: We keep some canned food for emergencies.
vocabulary.note_en: As a noun, "can" means a metal container (tin).

vocabulary.meaning_en: something bought for less than its real value
vocabulary.example: This jacket was a real bargain.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a list of things to buy at the shop
vocabulary.example: Don't forget to add eggs to the grocery list.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who buys from a shop
vocabulary.example: The shop was full of customers.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the material that a product is wrapped in
vocabulary.example: The packaging was hard to open.
vocabulary.note_en: pack = put things into a box or bag; package = a parcel.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a bag made of plastic
vocabulary.example: Do you need a plastic bag?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a bag you can use many times
vocabulary.example: I always bring a reusable bag.
vocabulary.note_en: use → reuse (use again) → reusable (can be used again).

vocabulary.meaning_en: grown without chemicals
vocabulary.example: Organic vegetables are more expensive.

vocabulary.meaning_en: products brought from another country
vocabulary.example: Imported goods cost more because of taxes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a label that shows the price
vocabulary.example: There was no price tag on the shirt.

vocabulary.meaning_en: black lines on a product that a machine reads
vocabulary.example: The cashier scanned the barcode.

vocabulary.meaning_en: people waiting one behind the other
vocabulary.example: We waited in the queue for ten minutes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a fast checkout for people with few items
vocabulary.example: Use the express lane if you have fewer than ten items.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the goods a shop has available
vocabulary.note_ar: in stock = متوفر، out of stock = نفد
vocabulary.example: Sorry, that size is out of stock.
vocabulary.note_en: in stock = available; out of stock = sold out.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the last date a product is good to use
vocabulary.example: Always check the expiry date on milk.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a card that collects points when you shop
vocabulary.example: I paid and scanned my loyalty card.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not able to focus because of something else
vocabulary.example: He was distracted by his phone.
vocabulary.note_en: distracted by = unable to focus because of something.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to disagree with someone angrily
vocabulary.example: They argued about the last seat.
vocabulary.note_en: Pattern: argue with someone about something.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to take something quickly
vocabulary.example: She grabbed her keys and ran out.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to move or act quickly
vocabulary.example: We hurried to catch the bus.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in a tidy, organised way
vocabulary.example: The books were neatly arranged.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to go somewhere quietly so no one notices
vocabulary.example: He sneaked into the room late.
vocabulary.note_en: sneak into = go into a place quietly and secretly.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to pass something under a reader
vocabulary.example: The cashier scanned my items.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to proudly let others see something
vocabulary.example: He showed off his new phone.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to slide a card through a machine
vocabulary.example: Swipe your card here, please.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to suddenly understand or notice
vocabulary.example: I realised I had left my wallet at home.

fine_lines.title: aisle vs lane
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلتا الكلمتين تعني ممراً. lane ممر محدد بخطوط مرسومة على الأرض (حارات الطريق، حارات المسبح، مسارات الدفع). aisle ممر بين أشياء قائمة مثل الرفوف أو المقاعد (في السوبر ماركت، الطائرة، السينما).

examples.sentence: Stay in the left lane on the highway.
She is swimming in lane three.
The pasta is in aisle four.
I prefer an aisle seat on the plane.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean a path or passage. A lane is marked by lines on the ground (road lanes, swimming pool lanes, checkout lanes). An aisle is a passage between things that stand up, like shelves or seats (in a supermarket, a plane, a cinema).

fine_lines.title: receive, receipt, reception, recipe
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلها من عائلة واحدة، ومعناها الأصلي «يأخذ / يستلم». receive يستلم، receipt دليل على أنك استلمت أو دفعت (إيصال)، reception مكان استقبال الناس أو الأشياء، recipe بدأت مصطلحاً طبياً معناه «خُذ هذه المكونات» ثم صارت تعني وصفة الطبخ.

examples.sentence: Can I have a receipt, please?
This is my grandmother's cake recipe.

fine_lines.explanation_en: These words are one family with the basic idea of "take / get". Receive = get something; a receipt = proof that you received or paid; reception = the place where people or things are received; recipe started as a medical word meaning "take these ingredients" and later became cooking instructions.

fine_lines.title: trolley vs cart
fine_lines.explanation_ar: نفس المعنى (عربة التسوق). trolley أشيع في بريطانيا، و cart أشيع في أمريكا وكندا وأكثر انتشاراً عالمياً.

examples.sentence: The cart has a broken wheel.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Same meaning (a shopping trolley). "Trolley" is more common in Britain; "cart" is more common in the US and Canada and more widely used around the world.

expressions.example: Two shirts for ten dollars? That's a real bargain!
expressions.meaning_en: a very good deal; something cheap for its value

expressions.example: She laughed to herself when she read the note.

expressions.meaning_en: pay and leave (a hotel or shop)

expressions.phrase: fast food in a different way
expressions.meaning_ar: مزحة: طعام يجب أن تأكله بسرعة لأن صلاحيته ستنتهي قريباً
expressions.example: It expires tomorrow, so it's fast food in a different way!
expressions.meaning_en: a joke: food you must eat quickly because it will expire soon

grammar.title: Past participle as an adjective
grammar.explanation_ar: الإنجليزية ما فيها «اسم مفعول» مثل العربية، فنستخدم التصريف الثالث للفعل كصفة: freeze → frozen (مجمّد)، paint → painted (مدهون)، break → broken (مكسور).
grammar.explanation_en: English uses the past participle (the third form of the verb) as an adjective to describe something that had an action done to it: freeze → frozen, paint → painted, break → broken.

grammar.title: Noun (one word) vs phrasal verb (two words)
grammar.explanation_ar: بعض الأسماء التي تنتهي بحرف جر مثل out أو up يمكن أن تكون فعلاً مركباً. كاسم تُكتب كلمة واحدة، وكفعل تُكتب كلمتين.
examples: The checkout was busy. / We check out at noon.
I did a workout. / I work out every day.
Make a backup. / Back up your files.
grammar.explanation_en: Some words ending in out or up can be a noun or a phrasal verb. As a noun they are written as one word; as a verb they are written as two words.
